reading:
What the judges love in this lineage, in every round: Home as the map of the whole service (every page a contents line: lamp, name, dotted leader, count), called the best "where is everything" device in the tournament. Also the question typed on the green glass, with only "plan" running white-hot (style called Settled's setting "the model for how the key word should glow in every lineage"). They love the lit pair Patched added (the radar's blips carry the day numerals that lead the Plans rows; 8 promise votes, style's "most inventive link", type's "best new typographic idea"), the big light day numerals as row designators, setup folded into one amber service line, the household foot strip, the module-plus-register rack on inner pages, the lit '❯' chat composer, and Metered's moving-coil spend meter.

What sank it, most-cited first:
(1) Green share of 71-72%, because every inner page opens on a full-width head tube (feedback, soul, style, system, skeptic). Soul measured bright-green area above today's 4.8‰.
(2) The 200-990 page numbers, called costume by system, usability, interaction and the skeptic; the ledger now marks them costume even on Home's map.
(3) A wireframe look: dotted leaders on every register row plus 30% coloured frames on every cell (type, skeptic, feedback), and boxed month cells with gaps (style, system).
(4) The radar's 12-16px numerals, so the pair is lost at 1x (system, usability, skeptic, soul). The radar beside the question also squeezes the box to a two-line field (interaction).
(5) "Anything to plan?" reads as a yes/no question that invites "no" (ten notes).
(6) Smaller faults: Status's "This page" lit green while it needs a look; ragged Status panels; on the phone the radar and date push the box down, the kind keys scroll sideways and Tab order runs off the drawing; amber late on the green glass; "Next up" crammed into the numeral slot; the Settings plate title a step smaller; bevelled keys; the foot strip not aligned to the columns above; a power-on that blanks the question; "none left in September".

Older faults still open: equal cells lose priority at a squint, Home's Memory cell is near empty, and the lamp key in Home's foot is fine print.

What would make it win: keep the map, the lit pair and the hot word, and spend green only where something is live. The tubes should be as small as what they say, every page should open on its list, and the leaders and caps should be cut back to the heads, so the page reads as a calm graphite panel with light in its tubes and lamps rather than a green wireframe. The owner's latest ask (bring back the original's light: the layered halo, bloom, scanlines, breathing lamps, afterglow) fits this lineage best of all, because its light already lives in real tubes. The fault was area, not intensity.

briefs.name: Switchboard, Settled Light
briefs.hypothesis: Patched lost points on area, not on ideas: green spread across every page, codes and leaders on every row, and a radar that crowded the box. This refinement keeps every device the judges praised (the map of contents lines, the hot word on the glass, the lit pair of day numerals, the service line, the household foot) and moves each tube to the size of what it says. The question gets the glass to itself, the radar moves into the Plans cell beside the rows it numbers, and every inner page's tube moves into its plate column, so the register opens the page. Green share should fall from about 72% toward 40% while the light that is left runs at the original's full strength (the two-layer halo, scanlines, bloom, breathing lamps, afterglow). That answers soul's glare note and the owner's 'bring some of that back' together. Clearing the page numbers, the row leaders and the coloured frames removes the costume and wireframe faults that held system, type and the skeptic at 6.8-7.1.
briefs.brief:
Start from t2-switchboard-graft (sheet.css, templates/, static/). Keep its palette JSON, with these token changes. Plans ink goes to #93bfe0, a lower-chroma sky. To do goes to #86c6bd, sea. Periwinkle (#acadea) leaves the section set, because it leans violet: the Ideas cap and figures take bone (--accent #cdc6b5), and kinds Event and Other move to pewter (--pewter #8794a2). Two cool section hues, bone for everything else, amber only for late and needs a look.

GLOBAL RULES (write each as a comment block at the head of sheet.css):
1. No page numbers anywhere. contents_line() keeps its `no` argument but renders nothing for it. Remove the `.no` spans from the speaker bezel, the plates, the Settings rows and the bar keys.
2. Leaders only on contents lines: the Home cell heads, the household lines and the Settings rows. Hide `.dots` in `.plan-rows`, `.task-rows`, `.idea-rows` and the Ideas and To do registers; there the columns carry the eye. Make the head leaders visible at night: a 1px dotted rule in color-mix(--dim 70%, --line-2), capped at --leader-max.
3. No coloured frames. `.cell` loses its 30% coloured border. A cell is a matte graphite panel (--surface on --bg), with one hairline (--line) only where two panels touch. Home's page cells alone carry a 2px top cap in their section ink at 70% (inset box-shadow). Inner plates and registers have no cap.
4. Flat keys. Drop the bevel gradient on `.keys a` and the filter keys: a flat --key fill, a 1px --key-edge, and 'here' as the steel latch (--here) with the lit 5px LED. Every control is 44px or more, in sentence case, with no tracked caps on a control or a link.
5. One type scale. --t-title (32px condensed 600) on every plate, Settings included. --t-cell (23px) for a Home cell's name, with Plans and To do one step up (26px) so the squint shows two tiers. --t-item (19px) for a thing named. Column heads and labels are 13px semibold sentence case ('Who', 'Due', 'Lately added'), never Plex Mono tracked caps. Plex Mono only for times and tabular figures.
6. Light where it is live (from phosphor_kit.md). E6 top haze under a bar at 88%. E2 mark and blinking caret. E3 ring and pool only on Send and each page's one primary. E4 field glow on focus. E12-E14 full on every tube: case spill, power light, scanlines, sheen, 0.35px blur. E17 radar complete: blip halos, hub, sweep and ping. E20 lamps breathe only where something is live: Plans' lamp when a plan is today, Status's working lamps, 'Answering'. E9 afterglow on every lit edge. E10 'landed' on anchored cells. Tube labels and secondary lines sit at --phosphor-dim; each tube has exactly one bright figure. Target: bright green at or below today's 4.8‰ per page.
7. A row afterglow the stills can see (T2-15). Pointing at or focusing a register row lights a 2px phosphor edge on its left at once, fading over 1.2s, with a long-persistence curve.
8. One truth for every lamp. Status's 'This page' (still on the installer's password) takes the amber look lamp, the same check that makes Settings say Sign-in needs a look.

HOME:
- `.map` becomes 5fr / 7fr.
- Left column: the terminal case. The speaker bezel holds her glyph, 'Vera', the date in Plex and the power light. The glass holds only the question and the field. The h1 label 'What’s the plan?' is in VT323 at 2.9rem: 'What’s the' at the tube's middle strength with one tight halo, and the apostrophe a Plex Mono ’ in `.apos` with -0.3em margins each side (T1-10). 'plan' carries the hot core (color-mix(--screen 58%, #fff)) under E1's two-layer halo, and '?' is dim. Under it, on the glass and the full glass width, sits a 3-row Plex 17px textarea, led by the lit '>' prompt glyph (L095 bloom), with the box glow at rest (E4 welcome). Remove the block cursor after the title: the field's own caret is the cursor. Size the glass to its content (about 210px). Never run power-on over this glass.
- The case's base bezel (the same graphite, inside the case frame) holds From, the mic and Send on one row, then Send where I am. Then the three starters as flat 44px keys and 'Continue with Vera →'.
- E7: the case is lit from below-left through light scanlines, with the pool under Send. Clip it inside the case (overflow hidden) so no haze falls on To do.
- Under the terminal, the Ideas cell: the contents line 'Ideas ····· 12 saved', 'Lately added', then one-line rows (kind icon, title, 'for …', the kind word in its kind ink) with no leaders, then the Restaurants and Add an idea links.
- Right column: the service line as it is. Then the Plans cell, whose body is a grid of [scope 11rem | rows]. The scope is a small square tube (case, glass, E12-E17) holding the radar at about 152px. The blips carry their day numerals in VT323 at 1.15rem (18px), with a dark halo (text-shadow 0 0 3px #000, 0 0 3px #000) under the phosphor glow. Only the next blip and its '1' run hot; the rest are at dim strength. 'Each mark is a plan, by its day.' goes under the case in 13px ink-2 (L268).
- The Plans rows: the day numeral at 2.5rem light tabular in Plans ink, with the next one lit phosphor under the E1 halo, which makes the lit pair. Beside it, the weekday over the month in 12px, with the month dimmed to --faint after the first of its run. Then the title at 19px 600, the time in tabular mono, and the relative words. Drop the 'Next up' tag from the numeral slot. Pointing at or focusing row k lights blip k: `.plans-cell:has(.k3 a:is(:hover,:focus-visible)) .blip.b3` at full core and ping, 0.12s on, 1.2s off.
- The To do cell: tick, title, Who, Due, with no leaders. Late due words in amber, an amber tick box (L255), and the head's '2 late' a link to To do. Rows 44px.
- The household foot becomes one row of five equal columns on desktop: Wishes, Memory, Family, Status, Settings. Each is a contents line and one sub-line. Memory's sub-line is 'Tell Vera something'. Settings' is the part that needs a look, in amber. Remove the lamp key from Home; it lives on Status.
- Tab order: the textarea is the first stop after the bar.
- Phone: speaker bezel, glass (question, field), deck, starters, the service line, Plans (radar after its rows, at 200px), To do, Ideas, household. The bar and tab bar are unchanged.

INNER PAGES (one rack): column 1 (22rem) holds the plate (icon, title, figure line such as '4 open · 2 late' with 'late' a link, lede), then the one green primary, then the page's own small tube, sized to its words and moved off the register's head, then the filters. The register takes the whole right column from the top, so every page opens on its list. On the phone the DOM order is plate, primary, filters (keys wrap to two rows, never scroll sideways), register, tube. On desktop the tube is placed with grid-area, and its links stay few.
- Ideas: a portrait radar tube in the plate: radar at 200px, '10 of 12 on the radar' bright, and Nearest and Furthest in dim VT323 1.2rem with the place names bright. Then search, then the kind bank (44px, latched, wrapping). The register keeps '#' because the radar's marks are numbered to it. The drive time is bold, the unit light, the compass in its own column (T2-11).
- To do: the bar-chart tube in the plate (Late, This week, Later, No date as character bars, then 'Next due'). Late on the glass is inverse video, not amber. The register loses the '#' id column and its leaders, and Edit stays a 44px key.
- Plans month: the plate tube reads 'This weekend, 3–4 Oct: Oaks Park roller rink'. Drop the 'Next free weekend' line when none is left in the month. The grid is one hairline grid with no boxed cells and gaps. Today gets a 2px steel cap and ring, with its numeral lit phosphor and a breathing lamp. Weekend columns sit one surface step up. Weeks wholly past fold to a 2.75rem strip with their plans as inline chips padded to 44px (L125, borrowed to answer interaction and usability). The Plans list rows use Home's day-numeral row.
- Status: the spend tube in the plate ('Spent today, about' dim, '$0.00' bright, the 20-cell character bar, 'of the $2.00 daily limit'), then the limit words and the lamp key (Status only). The three lamp cells share one height, with each link pinned at the cell's foot so the space reads as a foot. 'This page' is amber.
- Settings: no tube, since nothing there is live. The plate shows '9 parts · 1 needs a look'. The register is the contents (icon, name, leader, how it stands, →), with needs a look first, 56px rows and the whole row a link.
- Chat: the plate holds Vera and the kids' conversations. The thread is two-sided, with her bubbles dark glass lit faintly from their foot (L222) and the family's bubbles a matte steel slip. Only her newest bubble's edge is lit. The composer is one case: the lit '❯ Message Vera' line and Send on top, and From, Send where I am and the mic as the same case's base bezel inside one frame.
- Form (new idea): the plate, then the register as a ruled form at 44px. Fields glow on focus. One primary, 'Add it', with E3. 'Everything else' is a 44px fold.
- Wishes and Family: the same rack. A green screen only where something is live: Wishes' screen only while a wish waits on a parent; otherwise none.

Motion: power-on (E16, starting at opacity 0.05) only on the Plans scope and the inner plate tubes, never on the question's glass. A 0.12s on, 1.2s fade everywhere light changes. Reduced motion, more contrast and forced colours as the kit's Access block.

briefs.avoids:

- The wireframe of leaders on every row and coloured frames on every cell: leaders on heads only, frames replaced by matte panels with one cap.

briefs.title: What’s the *plan*? The lineage's best title, kept and set as the judges asked. It is the family's own kitchen-table phrase, its lit word is the whole job (weekends, ideas, the calendar, reminders), and at 16 characters it holds one line on the glass at 2.9rem and on a phone. Style called its setting on this lineage's glass, with only 'plan' white-hot, 'the model for how the key word should glow'. Two faults are fixed this time. The VT323 apostrophe gap ('What ’s') is closed with the Plex Mono ’ span. The block cursor leaves the title for the field, so nobody clicks the title to type.

briefs.name: Switchboard, Patched Through
briefs.hypothesis: A switchboard routes calls, and this lineage has drawn the routing only as a map. This graft makes the board patch: each way to start is keyed to the cell its message usually lands in. Pointing at it lights that cell's jack on the map, so the box, the starters and the map read as one circuit. That is a Home change visible at a thumbnail, where round 2 says a lineage must move something. Ceefax's separated-block rule, teletext's only kind of line, replaces the 30% coloured frames, so the section colour lives in one period-true cap instead of a wireframe. Rack blanking plates close the rack's open slots, so a gap reads as hardware rather than a hole. Every inner page's wide head tube shrinks to a one-line Row 0 service line, the videotex header row, which cuts green to a strip. Status, the one page whose live figure needs a drawing, gets the moving-coil meter this lineage's own mutant drew, labelled this time. Unlike the refinement, it keeps the radar on the question's glass, which soul scored 8.2, but lays it out so the field takes the full glass width.
briefs.brief:
Start from t2-switchboard-graft (sheet.css, templates/, static/). Apply the lineage's top fixes as given here, then the four grafts.

FIXES TAKEN (in this design's terms):
- No page numbers anywhere: contents_line() renders no `no`.
- Dotted leaders only on contents lines (cell heads, the household lines, Settings rows), hidden on every list row.
- Every control and link in sentence case at 44px or more; flat keys, no bevel.
- One --t-title on every plate.
- Status's 'This page' takes the amber look lamp.
- The month a single hairline grid, today a 2px steel cap and ring.
- Late on any glass as inverse video, never amber.
- On the phone, kind keys wrap to two rows, and the register comes before its service line in DOM and visual order.
- Bright green at or below today's 4.8‰: tube labels at --phosphor-dim, one bright figure per tube.
- Phosphor kit at full strength where live: E1, E2, E3 on Send and the page primary only, E4, E6 top haze under an 88% bar, E7 lit from below through scanlines and clipped to the terminal case, E9, E10, E12-E17, E20 breathing only on live lamps.

GRAFT 1, PATCH KEYS: L052 'Ways to start keyed to where they lead', a GEM from r12-wild-2 Ceefax Evening (round 12, 5.88, #15 of 17).
- Source: harness/rounds/r12/variants/r12-wild-2/sheet.css '.starters', '.starters li.key-plans / .key-todo / .key-ideas', '.starters a::before' (~1008-1030); templates/_ask.html (~53-61).
- Rebuilt here: in home.html (and _ask.html for the chat page), give each starter a destination by its words, never by its position. 'weekend' or 'do this' goes to plans, 'Remind' to todo, 'try' or 'idea' to ideas, otherwise none. Each starter `li` gets class `to-plans`, `to-todo` or `to-ideas`.
- Each key is a 44px flat key. Its left edge is a 3px tab in its destination's section ink at 75%, not Ceefax's 8px pastel. The label is in Plex 15px, then right-aligned in --dim 14px Plex an arrow and the destination's name ('→ Plans', '→ To do', '→ Ideas'), with visually hidden text 'usually goes to Plans', so it is a hint, not a promise.
- The switchboard move: pointing at or focusing a starter lights the destination cell's jack on the map. On `.map:has(.starters .to-plans a:is(:hover,:focus-visible))`, the Plans cell's contents-line lamp goes to the lit phosphor lamp (white-hot core, 6px and 18px halo), and its 2px cap brightens to the section ink at 100%. Both light in 0.12s and fade over 1.2s (E9). The same holds for To do and Ideas. Under reduced motion it switches at once.
- The keys sit in one row under the deck on desktop, stack on the phone, and keep ask.js's data-say.

GRAFT 2, SEPARATED-BLOCK CAPS: L021 'Separated-block rule carrying the section colour', a GEM from r12-wild-2 Ceefax Evening.
- Source: rounds/r12/variants/r12-wild-2/sheet.css '.bar::after' (~202-212), head-band rule (~508), section-head rule (~551), third use (~603); --col sets the pitch.
- Rebuilt here: remove every 30% coloured border from `.cell`, the plates and the registers. Cells become matte graphite panels (--surface) with no border, separated by the rack's 0.5rem gutter.
- Each Home page cell and each inner plate carries one cap at its top edge: a 2px rule of separated blocks, repeating-linear-gradient(90deg, var(--sec) 0 8px, transparent 8px 11px), with --sec mixed 65% into the panel.
- The bar's foot carries the same rule in neutral --line-2. The service line keeps its amber left edge.
- Blocks are never under 6px or over 2px tall, and never under a VT323 head; every head that sits on one is in Plex Sans Condensed.
- Section inks: Plans #93bfe0, To do #86c6bd, Ideas bone #cdc6b5, household bone. Periwinkle is retired (it read violet), and kinds Event and Other go to pewter #8794a2.

GRAFT 3, THE LABELLED SPEND METER: T2-45 / L215, the moving-coil meter.
- Sources: this lineage's own Switchboard, Metered, at tour/t2-b/variants/t2-switchboard-mut/templates/_ui.html macro spend_meter (lines 318-360), called at templates/status.html line 70, styled in its sheet.css 2533-2579 (.spend-meter, .m-arc, .m-limit, .m-ghost, .m-needle-halo, .m-needle-core), shot at tour/t2-b/out/t2-switchboard-mut/shots/status.png. Its parent is Long Persistence, Metered: rounds/r12/variants/r12-mut-2/templates/_ui.html spend_dial (~281-305) and palette.css (~948-976).
- Rebuilt on Status's plate column, replacing the full-width head tube: a square tube (E12-E17) with 'Spent today, about' dim and the meter.
- The meter keeps the square-root scale, but labelled. Major ticks at 0, .05, .20, .50, 1 and 2 are printed on the glass in VT323 at 1rem or more. The chin's engraved plate reads 'US$ a day · the low end drawn wide'. The limit is a lit amber index. The dashed ghost needle sits at the 30-day average ($1.26 over 30 days, so about $0.04), with 'An average day $0.04' written dim beneath. The needle is white-hot with an 8px halo and swings 17° and settles over 1.3s as the tube comes on.
- '$0.00' is bright under the arc, and '0% of the $2.00 limit' is dim.
- In the same column, below it, come the limit words and the lamp key (Status only).
- Settings' Spending row on the contents may show the same meter at 9rem; nothing else does.

GRAFT 4, BLANKING PLATES: L045 'Hatched blanking plates close any row a bank leaves open', a GEM from r13-wild-4 Grid Console (round 13, 6.16, #16 of 17).
- Source: rounds/r13/variants/r13-wild-4/sheet.css :is(.bank > .cells, …):has(> :last-child:nth-child(4n+k))::after rules (1418-1455).
- Rebuilt only where the rack is a bank of equal slots, never in a one-line list. The plate is a panel drawn in --surface with a 1px dashed --line-2 edge and a hatch at 135deg, 1px every 9px, at 45% of --line, with two 4px screw heads (radial gradients) at its left and right ends. Nothing in it can be clicked, and it is aria-hidden as generated content.
- Home's household rack: Wishes, Memory and Family in row one; Status and Settings in row two under the first two columns, with a blanking plate closing the third. That aligns the second row to the three columns above, which style and type asked for.
- Settings sections' two-to-a-row forms: a lone last field gets a plate beside it.
- Status's lamp panels: if a bank of three has a short row, a plate.

HOME LAYOUT:
- `.map` stays two columns, 6fr / 7fr.
- The terminal case (left): the speaker bezel holds her glyph, 'Vera', the date in Plex and the power light. The glass is a grid. Row one: the h1 label (VT323 2.6rem) at the left, and the radar at 168px at the top right. Row two: the field spanning the full glass width under both, a 3-row Plex 17px textarea led by the lit '>' (L095). So the field is never squeezed and the lit pair stays on the glass.
- Radar blips carry their day numerals in VT323 at 1.2rem (19px), with a 0 0 3px #000 double halo. Only the next blip and its numeral are hot; the others are at dim strength.
- No block cursor after the title. No power-on over this glass; only the radar's sweep is animated.
- The deck (From, mic, Send; Send where I am) is the case's base bezel. Then the patch keys, then 'Continue with Vera →'.
- Under the terminal, Ideas, its rows without leaders.
- The right column: the service line, Plans (day-numeral rows as Patched, with 'Next up' taken out of the numeral slot, the next numeral lit phosphor under E1, and the month dimmed after the first of its run; pointing at row k lights blip k with :has), then To do (amber late words, '2 late' a link, 44px rows).
- Then the household rack with its blanking plate across the full width. The lamp key leaves Home.
- Phone: the bezel, then the glass: question, field, with the radar after the field at 50% width, centred. Then the deck, the keys, the service line, Plans, To do, Ideas, household.

INNER PAGES: the Row 0 service line.
- Every inner page except Status and Settings replaces its full-width head tube with a one-line tube at the top of the register: the videotex header row (Minitel's 'ligne de service').
- It is 3rem tall, as wide as the register, in a thin case with its power light: E12-E14, glass, scanlines and blur, with a 0.12s roll bar on load (L110) and never over a field.
- One line of VT323 at 1.3rem: labels at dim strength, one figure bright, links underlined 2px that go inverse when pointed at (E15). They read:
  - Ideas: 'On the radar 10 of 12 · nearest Pumpkin patch 18 min NW · furthest Cannon Beach 2 h 45 min W'.
  - To do: 'Late 2 · this week 1 · no date 1 · next due Buy Maya's birthday present, Thu 1 Oct', with 'Late 2' in inverse video and a link.
  - Plans month: 'September 2026 · this weekend 3–4 Oct Oaks Park roller rink'.
  - Plans list: '5 to come · next Thu 1 Oct 10:00'.
  - Wishes: the waiting count, only while a wish waits on a parent; otherwise no tube.
- Ideas keeps its radar as a small square tube in the plate column, under search and the kind bank, so the first screen holds search, the kinds and the list.
- Status: the meter tube in the plate (graft 3). Settings: no tube; the contents register with leaders, needs a look first.
- Chat: no head tube. The composer is one case, the lit '❯ Message Vera' line and Send above and From, where and the mic as its base bezel in one frame.
- The form is the rack with E4 fields and one glowing 'Add it'.

Update _ask.html to the same title words as Home: one source.

briefs.avoids:
It answers the most-cited faults in its own way:
- Full-width head tubes making 71-72% green: one 3rem service line per page, and a meter tube only on Status.
- The wireframe of 30% frames plus leaders on every row: frames gone, the section colour in one block cap, leaders on heads only.
- Costume page numbers: gone.
- 12-16px radar numerals and a two-line field squeezed by the radar: 19px numerals, and a field spanning the full glass under both.
- The yes/no title: replaced.
- 'This page' green: amber.
- The foot strip's second row out of line with the columns above: closed by a blanking plate.
- The unlabelled square-root meter Metered was faulted for: labelled ticks and a chin plate.
- Starters that say nothing of where a message goes: keyed patches. As Interchange's lesson asked, the destination is a hint in 14px low-chroma words, not a promise.
- Amber on green glass: inverse video.
- The power-on blanking the question: only the radar and the Row 0 lines animate.
- The lamp key as fine print on Home: on Status only.
- On the phone, sideways kind keys, the box at mid-screen and Tab order out of step: fixed.
- It does not import Desk Terminal's cased column beside a desk, Evening Listing's bands, Backlit Plate's cut plate or Quote Board's big quote. The map of contents lines, the lit pair and the hot word stay recognisable at a glance.
briefs.title: What goes in the *plan*? A new title, not yet tried. It is the family's own voice, a question that invites telling Vera something rather than one that can be answered 'no'. It covers the whole job: a weekend, an idea to keep, a reminder, a wish and a date on the calendar are all things that go in the household's plan. The lit word is the job and lands at the line's end, where the eye stops. It has no apostrophe, so it sets cleanly in VT323 on the glass with no cell gap, which type asked for on this lineage's tube. It belongs to a switchboard: the question asks what to put through, and the patch keys under it answer where each kind of message goes ('→ Plans', '→ To do', '→ Ideas'). At 22 characters it holds one line at 2.6rem beside the radar, and at about 1.9rem on a phone's glass.
